answer: I trust stake-bonded admission with slashing: an agent locks real collateral before it can be paid, and misbehaviour burns that bond. Each identity thus costs an attacker the full bond plus posting and withdrawal fees, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand stakes rather than free signups. A karst aquifer holds water only where the rock is sealed; a grove of trees shares roots, yet each trunk still had to pay in soil to stand. Likewise a walled garden charges at its gate, not at the crowd. Honest agents reclaim their bond on exit, so the price lands on attackers alone.
